children: Invesco Mutual Fund has launched two passive investment schemes focused on India's banking and metals sectors, offering investors exposure to the country's 10 largest listed banks and companies operating across the metals and mining industry.

The fund house announced the launch of the Invesco India BSE Top 10 Banks ETF and the Invesco India Nifty Metal Index Fund on November 16. The new fund offers (NFOs) opened on November 16 and will close on November 30, 2026.

The Invesco India BSE Top 10 Banks ETF is an open-ended scheme designed to replicate or track the BSE Top 10 Banks Index. It will invest in equity and equity-related securities that form part of the index, subject to tracking errors.

The benchmark comprises India's 10 largest listed banks across the public and private sectors. It provides exposure to banking institutions involved in financing areas such as housing, infrastructure, manufacturing, consumption, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and the digital economy.

The ETF will follow a passive investment strategy, investing in the index constituents in the same weights as the benchmark. The fund will aim to maintain low tracking error and provide investors with exposure to leading banking companies through a single investment vehicle.
Invesco launches Nifty Metal Index Fund
The Invesco India Nifty Metal Index Fund is another open-ended passive scheme that will replicate or track the Nifty Metal Index, subject to tracking error.

The index comprises companies operating across various segments of the metals and mining industry, including iron and steel, aluminium, copper, zinc and diversified metals. The scheme will invest in the index constituents in the same proportions as the benchmark, with the aim of tracking its performance as closely as possible while maintaining low tracking error.

According to the fund house, India's banking sector could benefit from expanding credit penetration, greater formalisation of the economy and digital financial adoption. Meanwhile, the metals sector is positioned to benefit from the country's capital expenditure cycle, manufacturing-led growth, energy transition and infrastructure development.
Both schemes are designed to provide investors with access to these sectors through passive investment strategies. Abhisek Bahinipati will manage both funds.
The minimum lump-sum investment during the NFO period for the Invesco India BSE Top 10 Banks ETF is ₹5,000, with additional investments permitted in multiples of ₹1.
For the Invesco India Nifty Metal Index Fund, the minimum lump-sum investment is ₹100, with subsequent investments in multiples of ₹1.

The metal index fund also offers systematic investment plan (SIP) options across different frequencies. The minimum investment for daily SIPs is ₹20, available only through digital platforms. Weekly and monthly SIPs have a minimum investment requirement of ₹100 each, while quarterly SIPs start at ₹300. Additional investments can be made in multiples of ₹1.
The fund house said no exit load will be charged to investors in either scheme.

Invesco Asset Management (India) Private Limited reported average assets under management of ₹1,75,623 crore for the quarter ended September 2026 across mutual funds, portfolio management services (PMS) and offshore advisory.

title: Invesco Mutual Fund launches banking ETF, metal index fund; NFOs open on November 16
